paragraphs.source_en: I jumped up, took my muff and umbrella, and hastened into the inn- passage: a man was standing by the open door, and in the lamp-lit street I dimly saw a one-horse conveyance. ‘This will be your luggage, I suppose?’ said the man rather abruptly when he saw me, pointing to my trunk in the passage. ‘Yes.’ He hoisted it on to the vehicle, which was a sort of car, and then I got in; before he shut me up, I asked him how far it was to Thornfield. ‘A matter of six miles.’ ‘How long shall we be before we get there?’ ‘Happen an hour and a half.’ He fastened the car door, climbed to his own seat outside, and we set off. Our progress was leisurely, and gave me ample time to reflect; I was content to be at length so near the end of my journey; and as I leaned back in the comfortable though not elegant conveyance, I meditated much at my ease.
